concepts.name: Sorting

background.summary: An undergraduate computer science reader who has studied algorithm analysis (big-O, recurrences, sorting, divide and conquer including Karatsuba-style multiplication), discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, gcd and coprimality, the Chinese remainder theorem in its basic form, permutations, binary representation), and calculus and linear algebra through matrices, Gaussian elimination and basic vector spaces. They know complex numbers and polynomials, and have seen simple Turing machines with tapes. They have not met the fast Fourier transform in depth beyond its name, finite-field or group-theoretic structure beyond Z/n, Kronecker products, or any research-level multiplication algorithms.
